artists.biography: Dead Cross emerged out of a series of impractical schemes, fallen-through plans, and last-minute musical experimentation. Shows were scheduled before a single song was written, fans were formed before even one show was played. The chaos of its creation seems apt; after all, the band is comprised entirely of artists who have thrived playing tightly-coiled turmoil—intelligent dissonance disguised as disorder. Consisting of Dave Lombardo, Justin Pearson, Michael Crain, and Mike Patton, the impressive, expansive, and eclectic list of prior bands collectively played in would be enough to ensure the unyielding ferocity of the music... but a resume isn’t necessary, here. Dead Cross stands on its own, speaks volumes with its multilayered evil-genius vocals, manic guitar riffs, and brutal rhythms. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Dead Cross is the self-titled debut studio album by the supergroup Dead Cross, released in August 2017 on Ipecac Recordings. The project brings together Mike Patton (Faith No More), Dave Lombardo (Slayer), Justin Pearson (The Dillinger Escape Plan), and Michael Crain (Merzbow) into a volatile collision of crossover thrash and experimental metal. Produced by Ross Robinson, the 10-song collection runs 27 minutes and showcases the band's commitment to angular complexity and visceral intensity, with Patton's distinctive vocal approach applied to what critics described as chaotic noise punk foundations.

The album received strong critical acclaim upon its release, with reviewers praising the band's ability to balance technical precision with raw aggression. Exclaim! awarded it a 9/10, while MetalWani gave it the same score, calling it "a hyper-kinetic joyride" that combines manic pacing with deliberate compositional focus. The Guardian and AllMusic also reviewed the record favorably, and it achieved a Metacritic score of 76/100. Commercially, Dead Cross peaked at number 180 on the US Billboard 200 and reached number 2 on the Heatseekers Albums chart, establishing the supergroup as a significant force in contemporary metal.

The album's success validated the supergroup concept, with critics noting how the individual members' pedigrees—Patton and Lombardo's legendary status in metal combined with Pearson and Crain's avant-garde credentials—created something genuinely distinctive. The record demonstrated that Patton and Lombardo could produce their most visceral work in their fifties, while simultaneously offering Pearson and Crain the opportunity to collaborate with their heroes, resulting in an album that energized the hardcore and metal communities alike.
